R1101.summary: Nicolò Sadoleto, Ferrarese envoy to Matthias Corvinus, to Ercole I d'Este: urging the King to join the league and take up 'questa impresa', for love of the league and to humble [the Venetians] once for all. Read at the time: the contemporary clear copy 7a; the files are partial parallel readings of the cipher against it.
R1101.en:
that the Queen herself is cross about something else, so that she does not care much about our business; although,
even if she did as much as was possible, she could not at present arrange things otherwise than as they stand, and
above all without that money; indeed she says that, even if she had been present and had done every effort for this …
[…] of an answer, that this one we have had through the […] if peace follows […] as she hopes, she will see to do and …

… to join and take up this enterprise, and not let this opportunity pass, which never was, nor perhaps will be, again;
and that he should do it for the love and goodwill, and for the very close affinity that he has with the whole League,
and for the honour and glory of His Majesty, and to humble [W01] once and for all, so that they would learn to stay
within their own bounds.

R1102.summary: Sadoleto learnt in great secrecy from dom Francesco that the Signoria of Venice had written to Francesco Quirino to offer the King of Hungary friendship, Veglia, and the captaincy of its fleet for his (bastard) son, with a yearly payment in ducats.
R1102.en:
Being in Buda, about to leave to come to Pozsony, I learned in great secrecy from dom Francesco how [the Signoria of
Venice] had written to Francesco Quirino, who is here, to go to [the King of Hungary] and make him the offer that [the
Signoria of Venice] wished to have good friendship with him, and wished to give him Veglia, and wanted his son (he is a
bastard) as their captain of the fleet at sea, and wished to give him a hundred thousand ducats every year; but it
wished to be able to hire soldiers and [U20] draw men from this kingdom. And His [U03] had learned this by a subtle
way, and would not for anything in the world have me show that I knew anything of it.

R1103.summary: A faded four-line cipher block; no continuous reading is established, only the isolated word 'vostro'. The file is the image audit, not a decipherment.

R1106.summary: The King 'ha firmo proposito de non se scoprire' and to avoid 'involverse in guera' with the Signoria of Venice.

snip.cap: ASMo Ambasciatori Ungheria b. 1/9 no. 8, Sadoleto to Ercole, Pozsony 16 July 1482: the seven cipher lines, from essendo in Buda to cento milia
snip.credit: Archivio di Stato di Modena, via DECODE R1102

system: Monoalphabetic substitution in graphic signs with a few homophones (a, e, n, o, r, t, u), word divisions kept, clear words mixed in, and some code groups.
